description: StellarPulse is a solo innovation team led by an aspiring space enthusiast and independent researcher from Dhaka, Bangladesh. Participating in the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we aim to blend NASA's open space mission data with interactive web storytelling and accessible audio-visual design—bringing the forgotten relics of the Moon and Mars to life for students and explorers worldwide.
summary:
Cosmic Relics is an interactive space heritage exploration platform.
It maps historic spacecraft locations and simulates environmental damage using telemetry.
It addresses the challenge by transforming NASA archives into an engaging, interactive experience.
It preserves space mission history through storytelling, visualization, and educational quizzes.
details:
1. The Challenge & Problem Statement
Over the past six decades of space exploration, NASA has left dozens of iconic rovers, landers, and scientific instruments across the lunar and Martian surfaces—ranging from the Apollo 11 Eagle descent stage to the Mars Opportunity rover and Ingenuity helicopter. While these artifacts represent humanity's greatest engineering milestones, their coordinates, environmental durability data, and historical narratives remain scattered across dense technical databases, making them difficult for everyday learners and visually impaired audiences to engage with.
2. How Cosmic Relics Works
Built as a lightweight, zero-dependency HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript web application, Cosmic Relics integrates verified telemetry from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, and NASA’s Mars Exploration Program into four core modules:
Live Spatial Coordinate Radar Map: Plots the exact latitude and longitude of lunar and Martian artifacts on an interactive grid. Clicking any planetary pin dynamically updates the telemetry inspector.
Environmental & Thermal Wear Simulator: Models cumulative surface exposure based on mission duration, planetary atmosphere (or lack thereof), extreme thermal cycles (-130°C to +120°C on the Moon), and cosmic radiation.
Accessible Audio-Visual Storytelling: Uses the Web Speech Synthesis API to provide one-click voice narration of mission logs and engineering specs, ensuring inclusive access for diverse learners.
Space Heritage Assessment: An integrated interactive quiz module that reinforces STEM learning and measures user comprehension of off-world engineering.
3. Future Roadmap (What We Will Build Next)
In future iterations, we plan to expand the catalog to include deep-space probes (such as Voyager 1 & 2 and Cassini), integrate 3D WebGL terrain elevation models using NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) imagery, and add multi-language voice narration to reach global classrooms.
